## SECTION 1 — Macro Context & Regime Alignment

| Anchor | Value | Tag |

**4-Regime Probability Distribution [Assumption]:**

| Regime | Prob. | CBL Sensitivity |
|---|---|---|
| Goldilocks | 25% | Favourable — stable NOI, easier refinancing |
| **Reflation** | **45%** | **Mildly favourable — lower real rates support REIT multiples; consumer spending intact** |
| Stagflation | 15% | Negative — margin pressure, multiple compression |
| Recession | 15% | **Adverse — mall traffic/occupancy shock, anchor bankruptcies** |

**Enterprise Sensitivity:** CBL is a **rate-sensitive, consumer-discretionary-correlated** high-yield REIT. The 4.83% risk-free rate compresses terminal multiples (the core reason the market sits at 7.2× AFFO vs. my 8–9.5× fundamental range). Reflation is the modal regime and is net-supportive, but the 15% recession tail is the dominant bear driver.

---

## SECTION 1.5 — Historical Base Rates

| Base Rate | Value | Justification for Model |
|---|---|---|
| Mall REIT 10Y ROIC persistence | Low-single-digit, cyclical | CBL's ROIC is depressed by leverage; I value on AFFO (equity cash flow), not ROIC, to avoid the leverage distortion |
| Cyclical NOI margin peak-to-trough | ~5–10% swing in recessions | Bear case applies a −4% to −6% NOI shock (occupancy + same-center), within historical range |
| Retail lease duration (conversion/lock-in) | 5–10 yr terms | Supports the **Contracted Visibility Floor** — AFFO is largely pre-contracted, limiting downside |
| Mall occupancy base rate | 88–92% range | CBL at 90.5% is mid-range; bear case floors at ~85% |

**Model deviation note:** I do **not** use a single-stage Gordon GDP clamp. The terminal multiple is derived from the equity cost of capital net of a 2% growth rate (Section 3), consistent with the Reflation mandate.

---

## SECTION 2 — Business Quality & Competitive Moat

**Business in 3 sentences:** CBL is a leveraged, B+-rated retail REIT owning a national portfolio of enclosed malls, lifestyle centers, and open-air properties, generating a contracted multi-year lease annuity. It has just completed a transformational de-levering (refinancing its $634M secured term loan to 2031, cutting debt >$33M and adding ~$30M annual FCF) that removed the primary near-term credit risk. Operational momentum is positive (same-center NOI +2–3%, leasing spreads +5.7%, tenant sales +4.6%), but the mall format remains structurally exposed to e-commerce and anchor bankruptcies.

**7-Factor Moat Scoring (0–3 each):**

| Factor | Score | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Switching Costs | 1 | Multi-year leases create tenant stickiness, but tenants can exit at renewal |
| Network Effects | 0 | None |
| Cost Advantage | 1 | Modest scale; malls are capital-intensive |
| Intangibles (Location/Brand) | 2 | "Only-game-in-town" enclosed malls in select markets |
| Efficient Scale | 1 | Limited mall supply in some secondary markets |
| Resource Advantage (Location) | 2 | Prime, hard-to-replicate urban/suburban locations |
| Process Power | 1 | Competent leasing/repositioning, not a structural edge |
| **Total** | **8 / 21** | |

**Moat Rating (1.0–5.0):** (8/21)×4 + 1 = **2.5 / 5.0** — a **weak-to-moderate, location-based moat** in a structurally challenged format.

**Moat Direction:** **Stable-to-Slightly-Narrowing** (e-commerce erosion offsets location scarcity; the de-levering is a balance-sheet strength, not a moat).

**Lynch Classification:** **Stalwart with Special Situation overlay** (turnaround/de-levering catalyst).

**Financial Strength Scorecard:**

| Metric | Value | Read |
|---|---|---|
| S&P Rating | B+ / Stable | High-yield; upgraded 3/26 [Estimate] |
| Debt/Equity (consolidated) | ~5.9× ($2.17B / $0.365B) | **High leverage** |
| Dividend Payout (vs. Adj. FFO) | 34.7% ($2.50 / $7.21) | **Sustainable** |
| Piotroski F-score | 6/6 evaluable | Positive |
| Accruals Ratio | −0.0415 | Cash-backed earnings (good) |

---

## SECTION 2.5 — Adjusted Financials & Lifecycle Economics

**Capitalized R&D / SBC:** CBL is a REIT — no material R&D. SBC is immaterial ($0.017B FY2025 [Actual]) and is deducted in owner-earnings below.

**GAAP → Owner Earnings Bridge (FY2025):**

| Line | $M | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| GAAP Net Income | 136 | [Actual] |
| + D&A | 165 | [Actual] |
| − SBC (economic deduction) | (17) | [Actual] |
| ± One-off gains/losses (asset sales, refinancing) | ~±30 | [Estimate] |
| **≈ GAAP-basis cash earnings** | **~314** | [Estimate] |
| **Adjusted FFO (company-reported, the correct REIT metric)** | **222.4** ($7.21/sh) | [Actual] |
| − Maintenance capex (est. ~$1–2/sf/yr) | (~25) | [Estimate] |
| **Normalized Owner Earnings** | **~$197M ≈ $6.39/sh** | [Estimate] |

> **Note:** For a REIT, **Adjusted FFO ($7.21/sh)** is the correct valuation metric — it already nets interest, G&A, and recurring capex, and is the basis of the sustainable dividend. GAAP net income is depressed by D&A and inflated by one-off gains; I do **not** value on GAAP EPS.

**Complete Value Cycle / Installed-Base Annuity Runway:** The portfolio's **multi-year (5–10 yr) leases** constitute the "contracted annuity." With 90.5% occupancy and positive leasing spreads (+5.7%), the re-leasing pipeline is accretive, not dilutive. I **credit the full contracted rent stream** in the AFFO base — stripping it out as "working-capital timing" would be forensic amateurism for a lease-annuity business. The ~$30M incremental FCF from the term-loan refinancing [Actual] is a **permanent** step-up (lower amortization + interest), not a one-time.

**Installed-base runway:** ~70+ centers, 90.5% occupied, TTM tenant sales/sf $453 (+4.6%) [Actual] → the annuity is **expanding**, not contracting.

---

## SECTION 3 — Valuation Synthesis & Triangulation

### 3.1 Explicit 5-Year AFFO Forecast (per share → $M on 30.84M sh)

| Year | Adj. FFO/sh | Adj. FFO $M | Driver | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY2025 | $7.21 | 222.4 | Reported | [Actual] |
| 2026E | $7.70 | 237.5 | +6.8% — raised guidance, Gateway Mall accretion, refi FCF | [Estimate] |

| 2028E | $8.25 | 254.5 | +3.1% | [Estimate] |
| 2029E | $8.45 | 260.6 | +2.4% | [Estimate] |
| 2030E | $8.60 | 265.5 | +1.8% (decelerating to terminal) | [Estimate] |

### 3.2 Discount Rate Derivation

Because AFFO is an **equity-level** cash flow, I discount at the **cost of equity** (not WACC), which correctly prices the leverage risk borne by equity holders.

| Component | Value | Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Rf (10Y) | 4.83% | [Actual] |
| Beta | 1.41 | [Estimate — vendor, window unknown] |
| Equity Risk Premium | 4.50% | [Assumption] |
| Base Re (CAPM) | 4.83% + 1.41×4.50% = 11.18% | [Assumption] |
| + Credit/Size premium (B+ high-yield) | +1.30% | [Assumption] |
| **Cost of Equity (Base Re)** | **12.5%** | [Assumption] |

*(Reference WACC for completeness: (E/V)×Re + (D/V)×Rd = (0.365/2.538)×12.5% + (2.173/2.538)×7.5% ≈ **8.2%**. I do **not** use this for the AFFO valuation — it understates equity risk because high leverage depresses WACC.)*

### 3.3 Dual Terminal Valuation

**First-Principles Capitalization Rate:**
Terminal multiple = 1 / (Re − g) = 1 / (12.5% − 2.0%) = **9.52×** [Assumption]

**Peer Cross-Check (empirical retail REIT AFFO multiples):**

| Peer | AFFO Multiple | Note |
|---|---|---|
| VICI Properties | 12–15× | High-quality, triple-net (premium) |
| BGP / PDU | 8–12× | Diversified/open-air |
| WPG (Washington Prime) | 6–8× | Distressed mall (floor) |
| **CBL (current)** | **7.2×** | Market-implied |
| **CBL (justified terminal)** | **8.0–9.5×** | De-levered, B+ stable, positive NOI |

The first-principles 9.5× is at the **upper** end of the mall-REIT peer band. I apply a **mall-format and credit haircut** to land the Base terminal at **8.0×**, Bull at **10.0×** (BB upgrade + multiple expansion), Bear at **6.5×** (compression).

### 3.4 DCF (Base Case: Re 12.5%, g 2.0%, terminal 8.0×)

Applying a **5% uncertainty haircut** (mall structural risk, AFFO durability) → **Base IV = $64.00**.

### 3.5 Reverse DCF — Market-Implied Expectations

At T0 $55.26 (7.2× 2026E AFFO), the market implies either (a) a terminal multiple of ~**7.0×** (vs. my 8.0× base) or (b) a discount rate of ~**14%** (vs. my 12.5%) or (c) **stalled/negative AFFO growth**. In other words, the market is pricing CBL as a **value trap with no re-rating** — it is **not** crediting the resolved refinancing risk, the S&P upgrade, or the positive operational momentum. **This is the source of the asymmetry.**

---

## SECTION 3.5 — Second-Order Effects & Reflexivity

- **Competitive counter-moves:** Peer mall REITs (BGP, PDU, WPG) are de-levering in parallel; VICI is the quality alternative capturing institutional retail-REIT flows. CBL's B+ upgrade narrows its discount to VICI but does not close it.
- **Pricing tolerance elasticity:** Q1'26 leasing spreads of **+5.7%** (new leases +55.5%) [Actual] demonstrate **real pricing power** in re-leasing — tenants pay up for "only-game-in-town" locations. This is a positive second-order: re-leasing at higher rents compounds the annuity.
- **Balance-sheet reflexivity (positive loop):** Refinancing → +$30M FCF → +39% dividend → higher equity credibility → easier future refinancing at lower spreads → further de-levering. The S&P upgrade to B+/Stable [Estimate] is the trigger that unlocks this loop. **Risk:** if the loop stalls (occupancy decline), the reverse spiral (higher spreads → less FCF → lower dividend) is the bear transmission.

---

## SECTION 4 — Scenarios & Bounded Distributions

**Contracted Visibility Floor:** CBL's AFFO is **>85% contracted** via multi-year leases. Per the Charter, the Bear case **cannot** model revenue/margins below the contracted floor without citing specific counterparty cancellations. The bear shock is therefore applied to (i) **vacancy on the re-leasing pipeline**, (ii) **same-center NOI deflation**, and (iii) **a discrete anchor-bankruptcy event** — not to the contracted base.

### Scenario Table (per share)

| Driver | Base | Bull | Bear | Tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026E Adj. FFO/sh | $7.70 | $7.90 | $7.20 | [Estimate] |
| 2030E Adj. FFO/sh | $8.60 | $9.35 | $6.90 | [Estimate] |
| Occupancy (2026E) | 91% | 92% | 87% | [Estimate] |
| Same-center NOI growth | +2.5% | +3.5% | −4% | [Estimate] |
| Discount Rate (Re) | 12.5% | 11.5% | 14.5% | [Assumption] |
| Terminal Multiple | 8.0× | 10.0× | 6.5× | [Assumption] |
| Terminal Growth (g) | 2.0% | 2.5% | 1.0% | [Assumption] |
| **Intrinsic Value** | **$64.00** | **$80.00** | **$46.00** | [Estimate] |

**Bear-case causal transmission (bottom-up):** (1) Recession (15% regime prob) → mall traffic −5–8% → same-center NOI turns −4% [Estimate]; (2) a second anchor/tenant bankruptcy wave (Francesca's/Eddie Bauer precedent [Actual]) → ~150K sf vacancy → occupancy 90.5%→87% [Estimate]; (3) operating de-leverage: property opex is ~65% fixed → NOI margin falls ~200 bps on the vacant base [Assumption]; (4) cost-of-capital shock: +200 bps on Re (12.5%→14.5%) compresses the terminal multiple 8.0×→6.5× [Assumption]. **The contracted lease base (≈$200M+ of AFFO) does NOT break** — only the incremental/re-leasing layer is impaired. No bankruptcy fiction: CBL is a de-levering oligopoly mall owner with a 2031 maturity wall, not a going-concern at risk of liquidation.

| Case | Prob. | IV | Weighted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base | 0.40 | $64.00 | $25.60 |
| Bull | 0.25 | $80.00 | $20.00 |
| Bear | 0.35 | $46.00 | $16.10 |
| **Expected IV** | 1.00 | | **$61.70** |

**Confidence Intervals:**
- **50% CI:** $52.00 – $72.00 (Bear-to-mid-Base band)
- **80% CI:** $46.00 – $80.00 (full Bear-to-Bull range)

---

## SECTION 4.5 — Time Horizon Arbitrage

- **Market-implied horizon:** ~**0–12 months.** At 7.2× AFFO with no re-rating priced, the market treats CBL as a static yield vehicle — it is **not** paying for the 3–5 year de-levering → BB-upgrade → multiple-expansion path.
- **Fundamental compounding horizon:** **3–5 years.** The de-levering runway (B+→BB), the +$30M permanent FCF step-up, and accretive re-leasing (+5.7% spreads) compound the AFFO base and justify a re-rating from 7.2× to 8.5–9.5×.
- **Arbitrage:** The market is short the **time value of the balance-sheet transformation**. An underwriter with a 3–5 year horizon captures the re-rating; a 12-month trader does not. **This is a horizon-arbitrage long.**

---

## SECTION 5 — Conviction & Positioning

**15-Point Conviction Rubric (0–3 each):**

| Pillar | Score | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| Quality | 1 | Weak location moat (2.5/5), structurally challenged format, high leverage |
| Valuation | 2 | 13.7% MoS to Base; 7.2× market vs. 8–9.5× justified |
| Macro | 2 | Reflation supportive, but 4.83% Rf compresses multiples |
| Thesis Clarity | 3 | Crystalline: resolved refi + S&P upgrade + positive NOI → re-rating |
| Execution | 2 | Strong 2025–26 track record (refi, asset sales, acquisitions); ongoing de-levering risk |
| **Total** | **10 / 15** | |

**Conviction Tier:** **HIGH** (10/15) → **Max weight cap 5–8%.**

**Conviction Decay Schedule:** −1 pt per 6 months absent positive milestone confirmation (i.e., by 3/27 → 9/15, by 9/27 → 8/15 if milestones slip). Decay to Medium (<7) triggers a position review/reduction.

---

Sentiment is **not** euphoric — there is room for a re-rating without fighting a crowded bid. | [Estimate] |

---

## SECTION 6 — Portfolio Fit & Role

- **Asset Role:** **Income + Special-Situation re-rating sleeve.** Provides a 4.5% dividend yield ($2.50/$55.26) [Actual] plus 15–45% re-rating optionality. Fits a "turnaround/high-yield REIT" bucket.
- **Correlation Risks:** High beta (1.41 [Estimate]) to (a) **consumer discretionary** (mall traffic), (b) **interest rates** (refinancing/multiples), and (c) **credit spreads** (B+ high-yield). In a recession + rate-hike shock, CBL correlates with HY credit and consumer stocks.
- **Risk Budgeting:** Allocate within the **high-yield/special-situation risk budget**, NOT the core-REIT budget. The 8% cap reflects the single-name credit concentration.

---

## SECTION 6.5 — Mathematical Kelly Sizing

| Parameter | Value | Derivation |
|---|---|---|
| p = P(Base + Bull) | **0.60** | 0.40 Base + 0.20 Bull — resolved refi + S&P upgrade tip the balance to long; 0.35 Bear retained for recession/anchor risk |
| q = P(Bear) | **0.40** | 15% recession regime × mall structural exposure + anchor-bankruptcy tail |
| T0 Price | $55.26 | [Actual] |
| Bull IV | $80.00 | Section 4 |
| Bear IV | $46.00 | Section 4 |
| **Payoff Ratio b** | **(80.00 − 55.26) / (55.26 − 46.00) = 24.74 / 9.26 = 2.672** | Expected upside / downside |
| **Full Kelly f\*** | **(p·b − q) / b = (0.60×2.672 − 0.40) / 2.672 = (1.603 − 0.40)/2.672 = 0.450 = 45.0%** | |
| **Quarter-Kelly f\*/4** | **45.0% / 4 = 11.26%** | Parameter-uncertainty haircut |
| Conviction Cap (High) | 8% | Section 5 |
| **Recommended Ledger Weight** | **8.0%** | Quarter-Kelly (11.26%) **capped** at the High-conviction 8% ceiling |

> The raw quarter-Kelly (11.26%) exceeds the High-conviction cap because the payoff skew (2.67×) is genuinely favorable. I **respect the cap** and size at **8.0%**, reflecting both the mathematical edge and the single-name B+ credit concentration.

---

## SECTION 7 — Risks & Institutional Pre-Mortem

**Core Risks:**
1. **Mall structural decline** (e-commerce, format obsolescence) — the dominant 5-year risk.
2. **Anchor/tenant bankruptcy wave** (Francesca's, Eddie Bauer precedent [Actual]; a department-store failure would be severe).
3. **Residual leverage** (~$1.87B parent net debt, B+ rated) — refinancing risk is **largely resolved** (2031 wall) but not eliminated.
4. **Rate shock** — a +200 bps spike compresses the terminal multiple and raises refinancing costs on the floating-rate $176M facility [Actual].
5. **AFFO durability** — the +$30M refi FCF is permanent, but same-center NOI could stall.

**5-Year Failure Pre-Mortem ("We lost 50% of capital — what went wrong?"):**
A 2027–28 recession crushed mall traffic; a major anchor (e.g., a national department store) filed bankruptcy, vacating >500K sf across the portfolio; occupancy fell from 90.5% to ~82%; same-center NOI went −6%; the company was forced to **sell assets at fire-sale (6–7×) prices** to service the floating-rate debt; S&P downgraded CBL to B−/Negative; the multiple compressed to 5.5× on a shrinking AFFO base; the stock fell from $55 to ~$27. **The de-levering runway was consumed by the asset sales, and the re-rating thesis inverted into a death-spiral.**

**Tail Risk Assessment:** **Low probability of total loss** (the properties have hard intrinsic/liquidation value; the 2031 maturity wall provides runway), **moderate probability of a 30–50% drawdown** in a recession + anchor-bankruptcy compound event. The tail is **fat on the left** but **bounded by real-estate NAV**.

---

## SECTION 7.5 — Correlation Risk

In a **stress period** (recession + HY spread widening + rate spike), CBL's correlation to (a) consumer-discretionary equities, (b) HY credit indices, and (c) rate-sensitive REITs **converges toward 0.7–0.85** from a normal-regime ~0.5. **Conditional tail risk:** in the 15% recession regime, CBL's expected drawdown is −35% to −50% with low diversification benefit. **Mitigation:** the 8% single-name cap and the High-conviction (not Very-High) tier prevent over-concentration in the correlated consumer/credit/real-estate complex.

---

## SECTION 8 — Monitoring Milestones & Leading Indicators

| # | Milestone / KPI | Threshold (Invalidate if breached) | Frequency |
|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | **Portfolio Occupancy** | < 88.0% (from 90.5%) | Quarterly |
| M2 | **Same-Center NOI Growth** | < 0% for **2 consecutive** quarters | Quarterly |
| M3 | **Parent Net Debt** | **Increases** YoY (de-levering stalls/reverses) | Quarterly |
| M4 | **Leasing Spreads (new/renewal)** | < +2.0% (pricing power eroding) | Quarterly |
| M5 | **S&P Rating** | Downgrade **below B+** | Event |
| M6 | **Adj. FFO/sh (FY2026)** | < $7.40 (vs. $7.70 base) | Annual |

**Leading indicators:** TTM tenant sales/sf (currently $453, +4.6% [Actual]) is the **earliest** traffic signal; a sustained decline below +2% precedes an NOI miss by ~2 quarters.

---

## SECTION 9 — Adversarial Red Team

**5-Bullet Institutional Short Thesis:**
1. **Malls are a dying format** — e-commerce has structurally capped mall traffic; the +2–3% same-center NOI is a cyclical bounce, not a trend; by 2028, occupancy reverts to 85% and NOI deflates.
2. **The "de-levering" is illusory** — CBL swapped a $634M term loan for $600M+ of new debt at 7.4–9.1% [Actual]; it is still B+ with ~$1.87B net debt; the +$30M FCF is refinancing arbitrage, not operational improvement.
3. **Anchor-bankruptcy contagion** — Francesca's and Eddie Bauer already cost 87 bps of occupancy [Actual]; the next department-store failure is a −200 bps event that the "contracted floor" does NOT protect (anchors are the traffic engines).
